newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, but off highs.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended slightly firmer Friday, after retreating from fresh three-week highs seen earlier in the session.
"Copper has risen for four days in a row, so it's not surprising it ran into a little resistance today," one trader said.
"But seasonal demand may mean the LME inventories may start to decline again in coming weeks, providing support for further gains," he said.
COMEX March copper ended up 0.15 cent at 102.30 cents a pound, after seeing a session high at 103.05 cents.
The COMEX January/March spread ended steady at 2.45 cents.
LME copper stocks fell 2,125 tonnes to 123,225 tonnes Friday, while COMEX copper stocks fell 218 short tons Thursday to to 29,269 short tons.
In the past month, both COMEX and LME copper had been drifting back from six month highs, as LME stocks recovered from six year lows.

But the prompt market remains tight, with the spreads backwardated, analysts said, and Chinese demand, combined with normal growth in the rest of the world, is likely to consume almost all of the extra copper coming on stream in 1997.
"Prices could possibly test resistance at $1.10, while support is holding at 95-96 cents," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
